title: The Largest Black Hole in the Universe - Size Comparison
beats: Largest things in the universe are black holes, with no size limit; promise a climb from tiniest to biggest
Scopes out how black holes work; the video is only about size, and it points to earlier videos for the rest
Start at the very small end with primordial black holes; mass of a mountain in a proton-sized sphere
Earth-mass black hole is about coin-sized; size is tied to familiar objects
Primordial ones are unconfirmed; move on to ones known to exist
Define unit: solar mass, then sizes given as city or country footprints (16 km covers Paris)
Tiny black hole bullying a 30-million-km giant star; scale contrast again
M33 X-7: 15.65 solar masses, 92 km, shadow on Corsica; accretion like water down a drain
Mergers: 142 solar masses is the size of Germany, with gravitational-wave energy comparison
Gap between 150 and millions of solar masses; the universe is too young for growth by eating stars
Quasi stars as proposed fix: black hole inside a star, radiation pressure holds balance; flagged as unproven
Supermassive tier: Sgr A* 4 million solar masses but radius 17 Suns
Misconception that a supermassive black hole anchors a galaxy like the Sun; 0.001% vs 99.86% mass, dark matter binds galaxies
Jets and accretion disks; Earth orbiting would see a Sun 115 times larger and burn in seconds
Cygnus A swallows planets; M87 shadow covers the Solar System; ladder with Solar System as ruler
Ultramassive tier; OJ 287 holds three Solar Systems and has a supermassive one orbiting it; TON 618 holds 11
TON 618 may be larger since we see it 10 billion years ago
Replays the full climb from smallest to largest
Behind the Lies: only a couple dozen black holes have good data; mass from Kepler with error bars; Schwarzschild assumes no spin
Standardised data from many sources; source doc available

theory: The video teaches scale by fixing the sentence template and a familiar ruler, so the viewer reads each new rung as a delta. It places one genuine puzzle in the middle (the gap) and one misconception, which break the rhythm and make the numbers meaningful. Rigor is deferred to a closing honesty segment instead of interrupting flow.
